Yeah, but we played him a lot so our guys are kind of used to playing against him. Um but again, great player. It's not all about just that one player though. That's what really stands out, you know, with him. And just just to pick two players, him and Roquan, you know, just their communication with each other. I think it's two Pro Bowl players that communicate at a really high level and allow them to do a lot of things at a high level. And then they have a lot of other guys along those lines as well. No. I mean it just feels like that's everybody's always in it until they're not and just just the players and coaches I think that are in the division I'm not surprised by it. >> Going back to free agency do you remember when you first kind of had Boye come on your radar? >> Mhm. >> And maybe your first thoughts of of what you saw from his tape in Seattle compared to what he's kind of grown into for you here. >> Yeah I think who brought him you know who who really started talking about him first I remember Al mentioned him our scouts mentioned him quite a bit early in the process as someone we really wanted to walk away with in free agency. When that started I I can't remember who started it I can't fully remember but really good fit in that he can do just so many different jobs in the run game and pass rush and the times he's got to drop you know when you're in a five man front you got to drop those guys and had done had done that in the previous scheme that he was in in Seattle and played at a high level and and knows what it takes to win as well I think that's just kind of the icing on the cake you know having having come from a Super Bowl team it's just I always kind of say this you don't really know the person though until you get him in the building get to know him and I've just been he's just he loves it loves being around here loves loves talking ball loves loves practicing loves playing. You know what you're we're get every single day from him and that goes a long way with us, and I think he's played at a really high level this year. >> How much is his versatility opened up defensively in the pass rush what you guys can do, whether it's inside, both edges, just kind of giving you >> There's no question. I think I think Boye is a huge part of that, in addition to a number of guys you can name that are in that group. I mean, we're really what, I'm to four guys in that room, and they all can do a lot of different things. They all help each other. They're very unselfish with you know, it's just not me, go get this sack. It's it's helping somebody else. I can think of countless times guys have made calls that they they do a job to free up somebody else to go make the play, and uh bull guys, you know, instead of instead of a certain type of rush so that the big play doesn't get out. So, I just I think it's a really unselfish group. I think that's a big part, and I think in the early part of the season getting a feel for how people are attacking us. So, I think you know, those guys on the edge are getting attacked a lot of different ways, and so I think it'll start to take shape on how we want to play all that, and areas we can just be better as a group, but um his willingness, you know, to to set an edge and win in the run game is is equally as critical as being able to rush the passer. >> What do you admire and respect about Ted Karras? >> Ted, what do I admire? He's all ball all the time. He's not all the time. He takes his breaks, but um for the most part, he's he's always on edge. Something's always really important to him um in the plan. I always appreciate that. He's always going to have something every week that's just really important to get this called or uh we got to think about this and and so he's into it. He loves talking ball, loves, you know, his dad's a coach. so I'm sure that's where it comes from. And you know, he's just one of those guys he's fun to be around because he just he loves the game and so as a coach you like guys that are into the meetings, they're into practice. he's got great body language all the time and when when you're in a team meeting and you're speaking to the team and you got a room of you know, 90 people in there and there's always those guys who are going to give you that positive feedback which is good when you're standing up there time after time after time and um you know, the impact he has in the community is tremendous. And and it's very unselfish of him to to give back to others in a very significant way. A way that you know, is near and dear to my heart because of of my family, my sister and so I just think it's it's really cool guys like Ted and we have a lot of them on our team that have impacted the community the same way that they impact the locker room. And it's just fun to be around guys like that. Makes makes this whole thing you know, you put in a lot of hours, a lot of time, a lot of stress, a lot of ups and downs but then you got really good guys to be around and that's that's kind of why you do it. >> How invaluable was he when you were I mean you were in the midst already building the culture when he came on board but his approach, his attitude. >> Yeah, I again I not not something I fully knew about him um because he came into the draft before I came into the league so not somebody I had you know, sat in draft meetings over. but I can remember my first interaction was outside of what would have been you know, the defense defense coordinator's office at the time and he was just bouncing from side to side as he was talking to me and I could just tell he's like ready to put on pads and go play and it was March, you know, and that was just my first interaction with him and I go this guy's ready to roll and it was it was good to see. >> Thank you coach. >> Thank you. >> Mike dropped first. >> What was that? >> It is all right.

I think um a lot of a lot of football ahead of us, a lot of the season is left and and um you know, while we're we're we're disappointed by uh the outcome and and how some of these games have gone, you know, we're not discouraged. I think we understand how good we can be as a team. Um we're doing a lot of good things. Um ultimately it's about wins and losses, so we understand that, but um it's not like we've we've gone out there and uh you know, we can't do anything. We can't move the ball or we can't score. You know, we can. We just got to got to be more consistent in it and uh make sure we're you know, for me obviously taking care of the ball. >> When you self-scout, do you ever do it Do you see things like I can't do this, I shouldn't do this, I need to do this? What do you see with your game? >> Um, yeah, I think turnovers are, you know, certainly the biggest thing. I um being smart when to take a when when to take a chance and when not to. Um, you know, I think that's that's uh you know, definitely the biggest biggest part of all the games. It's biggest stat in in in football is turnovers. So, uh um you know, I've got to do a good job with that and I think that's just playing and play out, knowing when when the opportunity's there and when it's not. And um I've got to do a better job with that. >> How do you kind of practice what you preach there with a a team like Minnesota where it's so blitz heavy? There there's kind of some urgency there. >> For sure. I think, you know, that's their their style of defense is to try to make you press, to try to make you um you know, think something's there that's not. So, I think it's it's uh being in the game, reacting, uh playing off what you see and and uh you know, preparation's a big piece of that, but once you get in the game it's about playing and and and reacting. So, um you know, I understand that. It's a it's a good defense, uh but we got to do a good job executing and um you know, having a good plan going >> Do you have a couple more? >> Wait, with Cam's uh obviously Chris being like what Shane was saying, "Hey, it isn't all on him." He was saying he has to shoulder some of that responsibility. Do you all feel that as players, too, where it's like things would be different if we all had closer games and done better? >> Uh absolutely. I mean, I I certainly do. I think um I think we all do, you know, and and uh that's the tough part about it is you know, your play and and the results of these games affects affects people. It affects um you know, people in this building and and uh yeah, so there's definitely a responsibility there and and you feel that as players and um you know, I feel that as as a quarterback, you know, you got to got to play well. We got to win. I got to put the the team in a position to win games. >> You with Chris now gone, obviously you guys got a soft contract. You thought about your future at all this week given that the GM and you had a contract talk a long time ago. >> Um I think um you know, biggest thing for me is playing playing good football like it is with with all of us in this locker room. I think um like I said earlier, um I don't think it's a time to um you know, think think about that, think too far ahead. I don't think we can afford to do that. I think we've we've got to play good football uh this week. We've got to prepare well, practice well, and be ready to go on Sunday. So, I think that's the approach I'm taking. I think, you know, we're all taking that approach. >> Is that something you guys are kind of telling each other, "Look, don't listen to the outside noise. Focus in and try to get it done this week." >> Yeah, for sure. Just focused on getting better and being our best this week. >> With Chris not being here, do you have any questions about your future? Do you feel you'll be here? >> No, I have no questions. I leave that up to God, and I'm just focused on being my best and giving my absolute all every single day and everything I do, and putting it all out there on the field. >> How much are you looking forward to this opportunity? I mean, they're undefeated this season. We know what's going on with you guys, but what a way to turn things around for you to win. >> Yeah, it's a great opportunity. It's a really fun place to play, great atmosphere. It's a great defense. It's a great team. And it's it is a great opportunity we have. And those are the games you really want to play in, so. Yeah, looking forward to it. >> You know Clayton, I know it's not totally up to you, but being here a long time, is this somewhere you would like to continue playing here? >> Yeah. I mean, I love it here. Met my wife here. Really appreciate and uh love this organization. It's it's been a long career here uh and made a lot of friendships and bonds here that I don't take for granted. So, yeah. >> Clayton, what did it mean to have the relationship you had with Chris Ballard when you started here? >> Yeah, I appreciate Chris a lot. Um Did a lot for me and my family and uh yeah, I feel like he always kept it real with me, which I always really appreciated it him. I remember getting a text from him my rookie year in the preseason saying right now you're playing like an average guard. So, that was just the type of accountability he had with his players and he pushed me to be even better and uh yeah, I appreciate him. >> Not just in this situation specifically, but when coaches or members of the front office are let go, are you players feel some level of accountability or like you feel like they played a role when the team's not playing well and something like this happens in the season? >> I think that's different for every individual. Um I feel like every single day I give my absolute best there's I have no regrets about the work I put in and therefore the performances I have given this year because I literally give everything. Uh that way on Sunday, whether I play good or what whether I play bad, there are no regrets. I know I gave everything I got you know, just learn from the mistakes and keep trying to improve every day um by following that process and uh getting better and leading as much as you can. >> And then part of her message on Monday was you know, as much as she felt like this was a move that needed to be made, she also feels like there's every reason for this football team to try to continue to improve and win. Were you pleased to see that part of her message as as much as it might have hurt to see Chris let go? >> Yes. >> And I'm not sure your your stance on like players only meetings or anything, but when things are going how they are and it's so hectic, do you ever feel the need to like get the guys together just to regroup? >> Well, it would be a players only meeting, therefore you wouldn't know about it, so yes. >> Hey, last one here. >> day that Chris leaves. would you describe just the general mood in the building right now? >> Um you know, I think a lot of guys had a great relationships with Chris. Um but you know, it's it's the same thing when someone goes down in the game. Like you have no time to really mourn or think about that. It's like next man up and we attack. We attack the next week. >> Are you off a little bit or what's going on with >> Uh you know, we just taking it day by day. Um it's definitely not as bad as last season. So I think I'm in a good spot for sure. >> Same leg as last >> Are you concerned at all about it being the same leg or is it just like bad luck this time? >> No, I'm I'm not really concerned. You know, I I trust our training staff here. And like I said, it's not as bad as last year. So you know, I'm just happy that it's not the same spot. >> Would you consider it like two separate injuries entirely or is it something you have to monitor going forward? I mean it's in the same muscle, but it's not the same exact spot. Like the same Looking at the MRI, that exact spot where it happened last year was like scarred down and that's taken care of. It just look like a different spot, but it's much minor than last year. So we're going to be good. >> What came back >> Oh, yeah. >> So how do you deal with these kind of situations? >> Man, you know, we appreciate everything Vallejo did. You know, obviously I probably wouldn't be here without him. So you know, I appreciate him for that you know, he was a great person. You you know, it's just one of those things where we just got to keep our head down, you know, stay focused at the task at hand because you know, um that's what he would want us to do. So you know, yeah. >> You know, you talked about you wouldn't be here if it weren't for him. That being said, as a player, do you kind of I guess if you're winning, he's still going to be here. Do they hit home to you and these other guys in the locker room as well that hey, we got to improve our play here. >> Hold on, say it one more time. The info. >> basically part of it is you know, you would probably be here if you guys were winning. And so, as a player, do you feel some responsibility at all? >> Oh, most definitely. You know, we we felt the same way when it came to like when I was in New York and you know, coach Saleh parted ways with the organization. Same as Joe Douglas, you know, so you know, as players we always going to take the blame, you know, because you know, it's win or loss base. So, um you know, we definitely feel that way and you know, we definitely are going to keep going to work. >> As a team overall, I mean, you hear the out and the outside noise all the time about hey, the season's over and over, but there's still a lot of football left to be played. Is that something you guys are telling each other, you know, as you get ready for practice this week that there's still plenty of football left here? >> Oh, yeah, most definitely. That's how it's always going to be. You know, at the end of the day it's always noise, whether it's a lot of good or a lot of bad, you know, you know, we just got to treat that the same way, you know. You get too excited with the highs and all the good talk and then when the bad talk start, you know, it hit even more or we just say stay grounded and then you know, it ain't going to affect us as much, you know. I feel like that's where we where we really at, so you know, we just ready to go to work this week. >> So, obviously, when you joined the franchise it was 7 and 2. To look up now and lose season with 2 and 4, like how do you kind of just deal with everything that happened since then? >> I mean, it's tough, you know, it's definitely definitely tough, you know, you know, obviously given the situation that I was in and you know, what I came into. Um but at the end of the day, you know, it's a blessing just to to be here and you know, um can make a great story, you know, we turn everything around, you know, uh had a highs and the highs, you know, and and accomplish everything we want to accomplish, so you know, we I'm very optimistic about it and you know, it's just it's a blessing to be here for sure. >> Shane said this is just shows you the crappy side of football and that's this is part of what you guys stand up for. >> Yeah, um I've been thinking about that since my rookie year. Like even just players, you know, some players get in, they'll be in here for a few days, and then they're gone in the next week, and it's like, man, like that's part of the business, but you got to understand that at some point, you know, and just, you know, focus on what you can control, and that's just doing your best every day and just coming to work, showing up. >> Do players feel some responsibility for the GM or anybody else getting let go? >> I feel like everybody uh feels responsible to a certain extent because during training camp, OTAs, we all were preaching like everybody has a part in, you know, the success and the failures of this team, so I feel like everybody feel like they have a a certain part in it, but uh like I said, you're going to control what you can and just go to work and, you know, make it happen. >> That's why whenever we ask you about do you expect to be here or not be here, you sort of then you just take care of your business and see what happens. >> that's that's really the only thing you can really do cuz at the end of the day, you can't control who's making the decisions, you know, you can just uh control how you're showing up to work, you know, what you're doing, how you're treating people, and just being the best version of yourself, and you know, the cards will be dealt the way they should be dealt. >> Hey, our Chris was always such a big champion of yours when we talked to him. What did that support over the years mean? >> Man, I always appreciate any support I get, you know, uh especially from a guy like that. Um his, you know, his position that he had on this team, you know, he believed in me enough to have me here. Um and I'm [clears throat] forever grateful for that, you know, I'm trying to, you know, do my part and not not make him feel like he made the wrong decision with me being here, so I'm just trying to keep getting better, you know, every week and just waiting on my opportunity. >> Do you think about your future anymore after Monday or >> I mean, not not necessarily. Uh any- nothing hasn't really changed for me, you know, I just got to come in, you know, do my job, um be decent on the uh practice squad, and just prepare like I'm the starter, you know, uh nothing really changed for me. I just got to be ready when my number called. >> Talked about not feeling any guilt. Like what's the hardest part about just the human side of this? Like when you know there's somebody who spent a lot of time getting to know you, your family and everything and then suddenly you're walking into his office during the weekend and all. >> Yo, like I said, of course it hurts because, you know, you don't want anybody to be relieved of any of their duties, especially a big position like that, but you know, we just got to stay focused. You know, we all have feelings. We all feel some type of way. We all were a little shocked when it did happen on Monday, but you know, you got to keep the keep the next foot going and just keep pushing again and just trying to make it happen.

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans, C.J. Stroud and Tank Dell address the media
text: some You're wrong. doing great. >> Nico, uh, obviously talked the other day about Tank and what that would be like, right? >> Like to kind of just see him out there. We were seeing him having fun. He's dancing. He's had a good time out there. >> Tank's been himself. He's always having fun. Always enjoy playing football. So, we're all excited about, you know, his process and his road to recovery. Excited for Sunday to see him run out of the tunnel. >> You've been talking all year about how well CJ's playing. What is like for you to see him be named AFC offensive player of the week? >> It's really rewarding for CJ to get that player of the week. It's rewarding in the sense of, you know, everyone seeing it across the NFL of what he's been doing, not just us, me talking about it all the time of how well he's been having an offseason training camp and all the way now to the start of the season. It's it's been that way, right? He's been doing a great job since he's been back and he's done a great job leading us in the games as well. So, I'm happy that he's able to get that rec national recognition that he truly deserves. How much more hands-on has CJ been with Nick in regards to saying what he likes, what he doesn't like, and you know, not forcing it, but you know, just being vocal about the process. >> The Nick and CJ's process hasn't changed. They've been in communication. I mean, last year they were in communication on, you know, things that CJ, like any offensive coordinator, when you're calling plays, you have to call plays that the quarterback likes. So, they've always had that consistent communication when it comes to that. your running back situation with David McGomery still sideline and now George Or Jordan injury. What can you tell us about what happened with Jaw because he did finish the game, played well and what do you think of Woody and uh Dari and Deuce's ability to carry the workload for you against the Giants? >> Unfortunately, Jaw did he finished the game and he had a a quad injury that that showed up when we went through our injury injury check. uh shows the toughness that he had to be able to finish the game, but he'll be missing a few weeks and you know, we'll continue to lean on Woody and what he see what he's able to do running the football. >> Um you you have a lot of unselfish guys in the wide receiver room. What do you see the benefit is having so many different weapons who are all really good at the same time um in the same What's the benefit of that? >> The benefit of our wide receiver room is we're going to put stress on defenses, right? Who do you want to, you know, put special attention to? Well, whoever you want to, whoever gets that special attention, we have other guys who are capable of making plays. So, the and it's credit to the guys that we have in that room and what they've done throughout their career, what they've done this year. Like, all those guys have made plays for us in the wide receiver room. So, I see it as a strength, a true strength of ours. And I see us like really being able to, you know, press the tempo and really put defenses in a bind. Do the Giants um changing quarterbacks change anything for you? And what do you think about JJ McCarthy? >> For us, it really doesn't matter who plays quarterback. For us, uh defensively, it's been about, you know, our process and how do we do things that we do the right way and do them well. So, whoever's at quarterback doesn't really dictate what we're going to do defensively. It's about us. We got to play better defensively because it wasn't wasn't good enough as our in our last outing. >> What have you liked and maybe you think you need to do better on defense? Yeah, for defense we got to tackle better to start. Our tackling was not good enough. Uh that has to be picked up. We got to eliminate the leaky yardage when we are breaking on the football. We are running swarming the ball. Guys, we got to get guys on the ground much quicker. We allow too many leaky yardage there, especially in the running game. Some of the short passes that are caught caught over the middle of the field, we have to secure those tackles. Right now, it's just way too many missed tackles. Guys are leaving their feet. Just poor technique. We got to play with better play style of putting our body on people, wrapping up, securing the fundamentals of tackling since middle school football. You got to put your body on people and wrap up. We got to do a better job of that. >> Allowed you to kind of use Logan um maybe on the edge a little bit. Is that is that kind of connected to where you can >> Those two aren't connected at all. >> Go ahead. Sorry. Um, how were you able to uh evaluate Sunday's game knowing that the field conditions were the way that they were? >> We got the win. That's that's how I evaluated it. We come away with the win no matter what, no matter the conditions. It's a lot of things that are out of our control. So, it's I don't change so many for me. How do you come away with a win? That's what happened. So that's I was asking because of on on Sunday the on the defensive side of the ball because I think that Jacksonville's head coach said the exact same thing about the footing and the way that it how slippery it was out there and how his was that did you see that when you looked at the at the tape as far as the defense is concerned? >> Yeah, I saw it in our walkthrough on Saturday on Saturday afternoon. Went and did our walk through. We saw the field conditions and how it was. We knew that we would be expecting rain. So you just have to make sure you put on the proper footing. It is what it is at that point. We can't control the field. We can't control the the weather conditions. We just got to make sure we have the proper equipment and be ready to go play and some of the things that you can do and can't do the pursuit drill, the fit, the blocking dummies, and of course, uh, doing that while you're in thud. How challenging is it to end season, you know, while staying up to not, you know, obviously going to injure anybody in practice, but you want to tackle better on Sunday? Yeah, we tackle better by not going to the ground in practice. It's just about putting yourself in better position to tackle when you're in practice. Whether you're in shorts or whether you're in pads, you can still square up, put your pads on people, wrap them up, and let them go. And we can practice in a in a healthy environment. We've done that for the past four years. We just got to continue to uh execute that in practice. >> You said you don't like the tackling. What do you like about the defense and what you've grown through what are week six now? What have you what do you like positively >> for us man been guys have done an outstanding job of stopping the run. I think our guys up front they don't get enough credit or Dline they've done a great job of stopping the run and they've continue to do a great job. Where we have to get better is in a passing game right we got to be able to make more plays on the football. We've had opportunities multiple opportunities throughout the game and we have to be able to make more plays on the football. >> How's Jaylen Petri and um is an update also on Reed. Yeah, Jaylen is still week to week uh with his shoulder injury. He's getting better. He's feeling better. Uh we'll see, you know, how the week continues to progress. And Reed is still in the prec in the uh in the concussion protocol. >> Do you expect Marvin Harrison to get more plays this week? >> However many he can handle. We got Yes, I expect Marvin his workload to continue to increase. I thought he got about I think he got a little bit under 15 reps in the game on Sunday and he handled all those really well. did a really great job. Uh so he'll continue to get more. Marvin, one thing I see Marvin is a very smart guy. He's picked up things very seamlessly and he's we're moving around a lot of different places on our offense. Guy our coaches can put him in a lot of different spots and he's handled himself really well. So he'll get more workload. >> How do you manage that? How how does the the roster construction go into when you got Tankdale coming back? That's adding a an additional wide receiver. Do you plan on carrying that many wide receivers for the, you know, healthy wide receivers through the rest of the season? >> I look at it as one week at a time. So, for right now, we're going to carry our receivers. And for us, it's how do we move the ball down the field? How do we score points? And we have a lot of guys who can be very dynamic with the ball in their hands. So, adding tank and with the numbers of the receivers, I I understand the question, but it's al it's a it's a good problem to have. I know a lot of people probably want a lot of the guys we have on our team right now. So, I'm thankful for the guys that we have. I'm thankful for the the ability that these guys have. And I'm I'm really, man, I'm really more encouraged by how great of a group these guys are, how tight they are, how they're working together. Like, when you get so many different guys in a wide receiver room and guys can be easily like, "Oh, I want the ball." Like, these guys are truly sitting on the side talking to each other, helping each other out with the offensive scheme and route. So that's what I love about the wide receiver room. It's it's no beef in the wide receiver room. Guys are still friendly, great teammates, encouraging one another, and that's what I love most about the room. >> Lester, what do you like about his ability to play inside when you do that? >> Toughness. That's the one thing that stands out with Kamari, man. He's still one of the toughest guys I've ever coached. So for a corner of his nature to be able to cover down the field, but also he can line inside the formation and go tackle, fit in the run, and be one of our most physical players, you know, on the defense. That's what I love about Kamari. I love his attitude. I love how competitive he is. I love how much he cares. And guys, been a I mean, a true warrior ever since he stepped foot in our buildings. I love everything about Kamari. and um you know being able to move him around. You have to be a really sharp guy. Kamar is sharp guy. We can do a lot of different things with him. So he's man credit to him for how he studies and how he's always prepared himself for both spots. >> Can you talk about Kan a little bit? I mean we know some of the um big plays we've seen, but he seems to make some really important plays. Talk about what he's meant to >> Kan has showed up and tremendously made some really important plays for us. I I tell the guys like, can we get him the ball where he doesn't have to make a incredible toe tap on the sideline or go but can we get him one down the middle of the field where he can keep running? But he's he shows up and makes I mean the most unbelievable catches and he makes them look routine and it's he's a quiet guy and they doesn't say much but he goes I was like man you know that was a really big play right but he's uh he's done a really really good job and CJ you could tell he's gaining that trust of being able to throw it to Kahan in the tight windows and he's coming away and everybody's benefiting from his play. How do you manage the the amount of plays that you want to run with Tank knowing that you know the process is still trying to see where he could fit when he comes to getting him? >> It's all about it's a feel as we get into the game. It's a feel as I mentioned earlier this week. It's no expectation like Tank has to hit a certain play number. It's for me it's and getting Tank back out there after missing, you know, two years of football. That's the the main thing like him just going out playing ball. I don't care how many reps he gets, right? But I'll have my Tank Dale jersey on on Sunday. >> You guys were the Giants just announced that JJ McCarthy was going to be starting. What is your impression of him and and in the Giants offense? >> My impression, first impression of JJ is watching the New Orleans game, just seeing right the the change of pace, seeing how he really sparked that offense. You just saw, you know, a different speed. You saw him making some big plays. He's throwing the ball downfield, really just cutting it loose. Um, you see the athleticism with JJ. He's in there. They'll design some zone read type plays for him to get out on the edge and run the football. But, uh, he gave that offense a spark, gave that team a spark, and I think they saw some belief from their entire team when he's able to kind of lead them back and have a chance to win that game there at the end. So, I see why they put him at the at the named him the starting quarterback. uh still a young player. He's still learning, still growing. And you know, for us, I always go back to us defensively. It's not so much about him, it's about us just playing our defense the right way. >> Couple of games now since you reemphasized the communication on the defense. Is that trending in the direction that you wanted this to go? >> Yeah, we're doing we're doing a fine job with the communication. Last one, >> along those same lines, if you can put your defensive coordinator hat on for a second, when you're down uh as many defensive backs as you are, how do you change up the game plan to give players that may not have gotten a lot of reps, you got a player that's coming off injury reserve, that's getting his, you know, getting his condition and things like that back. How do you change, not change the game plan, but how do you fit the game plan with those players that are being inserted into the lineup? It all starts with again what do what do our guys do well. So the guys who will be out there I try to put them in the most favorable position for them. Not I don't do it based on who we're playing and what scheme they're running. I do it based on our guys and what do I feel like their strengths are. And I just want them to go out play fast and be as successful as possible and not having to think a lot when they're out there. That's when guys play their best on defense. So that's my mindset going into it is always, hey, what what calls do you like? I don't have to run the calls. So it's about the players. What calls do you like and what do you feel like you can execute the best? >> All right. Thank you guys. Good. >> We were just talking with coach about the tackling. What are you seeing from a tackling standpoint and some opportunities to improve tackling and get guys down? Yeah, we have to be we have to have the ability to put body on body, drive our feet, um uh wrap up and bring the guy to the ground. I think there's a lot of things just um leaving our feet behind. Like I think the contact is good, but I think we're leaving our feet, we're just jumping off the diving board and not everybody get to the ball as well too. So I think those are the two biggest things that was some of the takeaways from the game is like man that first person wrap hold on and that second person come in and attack the ball but get the man down ultimately. We love it. >> With the Giants switching quarterbacks, I wonder what do you think about JJ McCarthy and does that change anything for you guys? >> Yeah, young quarterback. I think both of the guys we really watch tape on. Both of those guys can really move really well. I mean, they get out the pocket, they make guys miss, they make the first person miss, you win a one-on-one, you try to get Jamus down and Jameus is back there moving around, try to get JJ down. So, I think they're both very good athletes. Um, you look at JJ, I think he has the ability to open up a lot of more stuff. They want to do zone read, all those type of different things. Escape the pocket. It's going to be a good matchup for us. I think more than ever we have to rush together. He's a young quarterback, so we have to do a really good job of making sure everybody is owning their box. >> Will, I know that we ask you this every week, CJ Style question, >> he was awarded AFC offensive player of the week for his performance last week. >> Yeah. >> Was this just something that that you expected to see, you know, see him get these type of awards and accolades? >> Oh, of course. I sit right next to CJ in the meeting and I look forward to uh Wednesdays cuz I always want to know. But um he deserves it. You talk about a guy who's been consistent all year, um, leading the NFL in yards. I mean, leading this team to where we need to be at. He's playing outstanding, but it's it starts with his preparation. It starts with his process. You see him every day go through that same process, that same preparation every day on the field. So, it's no shocker that when we get in the game, he's making big plays. He's commanded the offense and he's taking over and winning these games for us. Are you starting to feel like, you know, even though, like I said, the record doesn't reflect on on everything, but are you starting to feel like it doesn't matter, as long as we got CJ, we're in a game. >> Oh, most definitely. He's a top quarterback in this league, and he helps us win a lot of games, and he is the reason why we've been winning a lot of games. So, man, like big shout out to him. Offensive line, too. Got to give them a big shout out. They held them those guys to zero sacks. Um, they moved the ball really well. So, like CJ had time to bake a cake back there. So, big shout out to those guys, too. Like, offense been doing their thing, and that's what we need. And it's awesome to feed off of that and play complimentary football off of that. So, it's been awesome to see, but I'm really happy for him because I know all the hard work he's put in. I know everything that he's endured up until this moment. And to continue to see his light shine and to see him bring this team together and go out and make those big plays has been great. >> Defense is going to get back not necessarily to last year, but to a level that you guys feel you should be playing at. >> Yeah, most definitely. Um, I I think the new thing every week, man, is just how how well can you be at owning your box? like every time we step on the field, how well can you be at owning your box and just doing your job. title: DON'T Count Out the Dream! Atlanta STEALS Game 3 at Home 🔥 | The Wrap-Up
text: Welcome to the wrap-up presented by AT&T. It is a dream start to this WNBA finals for the Atlanta Dream. A dominating wire-to-wire victory here in game three. Final score Atlanta 97, Golden State 71. Alongside Lorencia Moten, I am Sam Rabich. and we have the distinct honor and privilege to be joined by one of Atlanta's very own Angel Gray from State Farm Arena. You just took in the game, Angel. What have been your initial takeaways as this game just went final moments ago? Well, first of all, I was joking with you earlier just about the energy in the building, the takeaway from this overall was just more so because the fans were able to show up and then that really instilled a different type of confidence within Atlanta. I think me taking off my Atlanta chain for a little bit and being a little bit more unbiased. What I did see from Atlanta was a bit more of the decision making of Jordan Cannon, Canada, and Ryan Howard, who has back-to-back games with five plus steals that which is a record in the finals. I think another thing that I saw from them is Nas Hillman that was able to step up in a major way. A lot of the time she is overlooked because of what she does on the defensive end, but what she was able to do with going three for five from three, finishing with 15 points. I felt like there was a stretch in the third quarter where you didn't have to look at Angel Reese. You didn't have to look at Jordan Canada. You didn't have to look at Dana Bonner. Players such as Izzy Boulay's off of the bench, Nas Hillman in the in the starting lineup. And then there are a couple of plays for people sprinkled in as well. It was a a a win that was by committee and that's what this team has been built on throughout this entire season. >> Go ahead, Lala. >> Oh, yeah. I completely agree, Angel. I mean, listen to me, um, they left no room for doubt, the Atlantaer Dream did, as to whether or not they deserve to be in this game in the finals from top to bottom as Angel just talked about. It was won by committee. But what stands out to me, I would say, is how this team has grown throughout the series. You know, after dropping game one, the Dream responded with the win 79 to 65 in game two, and then they carried that confidence into tonight's game. But this was a very decisive win. I mean, for me, this one just felt different, and quite honestly, [music] I just feel like Atlanta wanted it more. >> Angel Ree obviously dominant in game two with that 30 point 16 rebound performance. Followed that up with her third straight double double here in the finals, 21 points and 12 boards. Angel, what's impressed you most with how she has played after getting held scoreless in that second half of game one? >> I think what's most impressive to me [music] is that when she says, "I want the ball," you give her the ball. Um I will say this after covering this team as playbyplay for the last five years, that has been the missing piece. This dog mentality of who to get the ball to and the fact that when you get the ball to them, they make magic happen. I will also say this, Angel Reese, every time she has hit a three all season, this team has won. So to see one early go down for her it was almost like last lights out.
